reviewed_hunks.quote: **Methods.** PRISMA 2020 systematic umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses, supplemented by landmark RCTs. PubMed (1,495-review corpus plus ten scoping searches), OpenAlex citation chasing, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Crossref metadata verification. 2,360 unique bibliographic records and 363 trial records were screened; 109 records (87 primary, 22 context) and 270 outcomes were extracted, including November 2026 updates of six gaming-disorder engagement records, three photosensitivity safety records, one gamification record, three incentive-design records, three goal-setting records, two retrieval-practice records, two habit records, one gamification-caution record, one planning-interventions record, two mental-contrasting records and one test-anxiety record. Certainty is recorded as reported by the source review; independent GRADE was not performed.

reviewed_hunks.quote: Two habit records joined the table: habit strength improves with intervention (SMD 0.69) but takes about two months to start forming, with morning and self-selected practice strongest (PMID 39685110); and habit correlates with behavioural frequency at r=0.46 through context-dependent repetition (PMID 21626256). Two mechanism sources stayed narrative-only: Lally et al. 2009, whose 84-day study showed a single missed day does not materially affect formation, and the 2021 habit-tracking guidelines. Implemented as R42: when yesterday slipped but the week shows prior practice, home says so plainly — one session today keeps it forming, nothing resets. The ~2-month horizon sets honest expectations; the calendar accumulates and never subtracts. A fortnight-plus absence gets the same treatment with lapse-not-relapse framing: a welcome-back notice instead of a blank slate.
